title: Strip unshipped quest-doc/lore-doc repository names from public CLAUDE.md
description:
User ruling, relayed by the orchestrator: strip unreleased/unshipped product repository names from public CLAUDE.md files -- fix forward, no history rewrite (git history stays untouched; this is about current working-tree content only). quest-cli's public CLAUDE.md named two: `quest-doc` and `lore-doc`, both former standalone repositories now consolidated/frozen into opum-doc's namespace.

Fixed: CLAUDE.md line 105-106 (outside the digest-guarded fleet-operating block, confirmed digest unchanged: 4cbdcba163ba318f before and after). Kept the underlying rule ("historical mentions... stay historical and must not be promoted into active instructions"), removed only the two names, replaced with "superseded-repository" as a generic placeholder. `salient-data/*` was left alone since the orchestrator's ask named only quest-doc/lore-doc.

Scope finding, not yet acted on: `docs/` contains 169 occurrences across 28 files, overwhelmingly dated ADRs, Stories, and reference evidence/research records (e.g. quest-cli-activation-gate-evidence-record.md, quest-cli-research-source-register.md) -- almost all already self-describe quest-doc/lore-doc as historical, frozen, or former ("the standalone quest-doc repository... frozen... routes to opum-doc's consolidated Quest namespace"). This is squarely the fleet's own "HISTORY -- completed records, dated logs -- leave alone. Rewriting a Done record to remove a word falsifies it" category. Sweeping all 169 occurrences would be a disproportionate rewrite of the dated decision-record corpus and would directly conflict with that same repository's own retirement-scope policy. Reported the true scope to the orchestrator before acting rather than unilaterally doing a 170-line sweep or silently skipping the docs/ check.

acceptanceCriteria.text: CLAUDE.md no longer names quest-doc or lore-doc as repository enumerations, with the underlying owner-checking/routing guidance kept and the fleet-operating block digest unchanged (verified before and after)

The docs/ scope (169 occurrences across 28 dated ADR/Story/reference files) is reported to the orchestrator with a recommendation grounded in this repo's own retirement-scope policy, and any further docs/ edits happen only per an explicit scope decision from the orchestrator/user, not unilaterally

implementationNotes: CLAUDE.md line 105-106 edited: removed 'quest-doc' and 'lore-doc' names, kept the rule they illustrated. Digest verified unchanged (awk over the opum:fleet-operating:begin/end block, sha256sum, cut -c1-16 -> 4cbdcba163ba318f both before and after; the edit is outside the guarded block, lines 140-315).

RULING (opum-agent, confirmed after reviewing the full 169-occurrence/28-file scope reported above): docs/ stays untouched. Recorded here so the next person who greps for quest-doc/lore-doc and finds ~169 hits does not re-litigate this from scratch.

The test: does the record describe something current and unshipped, or something superseded and marked as such?

- A record asserting a private/unannounced product currently exists, present tense ("X remains separate") -- a stranger would learn a live, unpublished fact. Redact.
- A record like this repo's docs/ occurrences -- "the former quest-doc repository," "historical, opum-doc-routed," "frozen... routes to opum-doc's consolidated namespace" -- describes something that no longer exists and says so explicitly. A stranger learns a resolved historical fact, not a current secret. Leave.

quest-doc and lore-doc were documentation repositories, not products -- the weakest items on the exposure list opum-agent was working from; the genuine unshipped-product leak this pass was chasing (lore-api, lore-mcp, lore-graph) exists only in lore-cli, not here.

Scrubbing quest-doc/lore-doc out of docs/ would not just remove a name, it would remove the supersession record itself -- the trail explaining why opum-doc now owns that namespace. That is exactly this repository's own Retirement scope rule: "HISTORY -- completed records, dated logs, changelogs -> leave alone. Rewriting a Done record to remove a word falsifies it."

CLAUDE.md (the live, currently-read instructions file, not a dated record) was the actual exposure and is fixed: PR #355.
OPAG-70 verification: confirming a hook-shaped write (using $OPUM_HOOK_ACTOR/$OPUM_HOOK_ACCOUNTABLE_HUMAN from settings.local.json post-move) actually lands, not assumed.
finalSummary: CLAUDE.md's two unshipped-repo names (quest-doc, lore-doc) removed, rule kept, digest verified unchanged. docs/ (169 occurrences, 28 files) deliberately left untouched per opum-agent's ruling: the test is whether a record describes something current/unshipped (redact) or superseded and already marked as such (leave) -- these records already say 'former,' 'historical,' 'frozen... routes to opum-doc,' so scrubbing them would remove the supersession trail itself, exactly what this repo's own Retirement scope rule protects against. Full reasoning on the ruling note above.
